---
title: "Readings — RNA libraries"
---

The papers below are the primary sources for the two decks. Read the methods first: each one is
an argument for a choice of step, and the exercises ask you to make the same choices.

## Strand, depletion and choosing a route

**Parkhomchuk D, et al. (2009).** *Transcriptome analysis by strand-specific sequencing of
complementary DNA.* Nucleic Acids Research 37:e123.
[doi:10.1093/nar/gkp596](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkp596) — **start here**

> The dUTP method as first described. Find the step where the second strand is marked, and the
> step where the mark is used. Everything in TruSeq Stranded mRNA and NEBNext Directional is a
> variation on this.

**Levin JZ, et al. (2010).** *Comprehensive comparative analysis of strand-specific RNA
sequencing methods.* Nature Methods 7:709–715.
[doi:10.1038/nmeth.1491](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.1491) — **start here**

> A side-by-side comparison of the strand-marking strategies. Look at which metrics the authors
> chose, and why strand specificity and evenness of coverage can pull against each other.

**Adiconis X, et al. (2013).** *Comparative analysis of RNA sequencing methods for degraded or
low-input samples.* Nature Methods 10:623–629.
[doi:10.1038/nmeth.2483](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.2483)

> Compares poly(A) selection, rRNA depletion and low-input methods on degraded material. The
> 3' bias figures are the ones to study.

**Morlan JD, et al. (2012).** *Selective depletion of rRNA enables whole
transcriptome profiling of archival fixed tissue.* PLoS ONE 7:e42882.
[doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0042882](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0042882)

> RNase H depletion applied to fixed tissue, the case where poly(A) selection fails. Note how
> probe coverage of the rRNA is treated.

## Small RNA and translation

**Hafner M, et al. (2008).** *Identification of microRNAs and other small regulatory RNAs using
cDNA library sequencing.* Methods 44:3–12.
[doi:10.1016/j.ymeth.2007.09.009](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymeth.2007.09.009)

> The ligation scheme for small RNAs in detail: adapters, order, size selection. Use it to
> check what you drew for the first exercises.

**Ingolia NT, et al. (2009).** *Genome-wide analysis in vivo of translation with nucleotide
resolution using ribosome profiling.* Science 324:218–223.
[doi:10.1126/science.1168978](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1168978)

> Ribo-seq. Read how the footprint becomes a library and where the three-base periodicity is
> shown.

## Tag and full-length protocols

**Picelli S, et al. (2013).** *Smart-seq2 for sensitive full-length transcriptome profiling in
single cells.* Nature Methods 10:1096–1098.
[doi:10.1038/nmeth.2639](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.2639) — **start here**

> The template-switching protocol that became the standard. Compare it with the original
> template-switching description for what was changed and why.

**Hashimshony T, et al. (2016).** *CEL-Seq2: sensitive highly-multiplexed single-cell RNA-Seq.*
Genome Biology 17:77.
[doi:10.1186/s13059-016-0938-8](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-0938-8)

> The 3' tag alternative with linear amplification. Find the step at which cells are pooled and
> say why it is there.
